title: Spread a fixed marked smooth proper curve diagram
statement: Let f:X→S be separated and finitely presented, and η a component generic point. Fix a finite purely inseparable extension K/κ(η) and a finite family indexed by Fin n, finite separable L_i/K, open immersions A_i→B_i with nonempty A_i and B_i smooth proper geometrically irreducible of dimension at most one over L_i. Supply a finite surjection ν₀:∐A_i→X_η×κ(η)K commuting with these structure maps, and an open W₀ whose inverse image is dense in each A_i and on which ν₀ is a thickening. Then this supplied marked field diagram spreads after a finite surjective universally injective cover V→U of an open neighbourhood U of η: there are finite etale T_i→V and diagrams Y_i→Ybar_i→T_i, with the same n, finite surjective ν:∐Y_i→X_V, open j_i, smooth surjective Y_i→T_i, smooth proper Ybar_i→T_i with geometrically connected fibres of dimension at most one, and an open W on which ν is a thickening and whose inverse image in every Y_i surjects onto T_i. This is a spreading result for a specified field diagram; it asserts no existence of that input diagram. [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-scheme-fibre] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] Moreover the models retain the supplied generic A_i, B_i and Spec L_i by cartesian squares compatible with j₀ and q₀; the base map from Spec K composes to its specified map into S.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood of η and replace it by its reduction. The reduction is a finite surjective closed immersion and hence universally injective; its generic residue field is unchanged. Apply lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-generic-cover to the supplied finite purely inseparable extension K. This proved limit-descent construction produces a finite surjective universally injective cover with its specified generic fibre Spec K, and avoids the original degree-p tower. Reduce its source; the generic local field remains K. Any shrinking O of this finite radicial cover containing the unique point above η can be realized by shrinking the original base: delete the closed image of its closed complement. Choose an affine neighbourhood of η inside that open; finiteness makes its inverse image affine. Later shrinking is handled in the same way.

proof.text: Express $k=A_{\mathfrak p}$ as the filtered colimit of $A_a$ for $a\notin\mathfrak p$. The affine-transition limit of $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ is therefore $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Apply the proved common-stage finite-family object descent lemma to the finitely many $Y_{i,\eta}$, $\overline Y_{i,\eta}$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k_i$, keeping $X$ as its already specified model. Apply the proved common-stage arrow descent lemma to their finitely many arrows, and the proved simultaneous equality descent lemma to their finitely many commuting triangles. These retain the supplied field diagrams by cartesian squares and the stated compatibility equations. A common later principal localization gives a diagram $\coprod_iY_i\to X$, $Y_i\to\overline Y_i\to T_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, whose generic fibre is the chosen diagram. Every object is of finite presentation over the affine base and hence qcqs. Every arrow is locally of finite presentation: on affine charts apply the cited theorem on finite presentation over a finite-type intermediate algebra. The supplied ν₀ is finite and surjective by hypothesis. Descend finiteness and surjectivity of $\nu$, openness of each $j_i$, finite etaleness of $T_i\to V$, smoothness and surjectivity of $Y_i\to T_i$, and smoothness and properness of $\overline Y_i\to T_i$, using the respective cited descent statements. Their qcqs and local finite-presentation hypotheses were established in the preceding step; the weaker local finite-type hypotheses also hold. There are only finitely many maps, so take common refinements successively. Finiteness and surjectivity persist by their base-change lemmas, smoothness and open immersion by the eventual conclusions of the two new descent statements; etaleness is smooth relative dimension zero and is unchanged under restriction of base. Properness, defined using the diagonal and universal closedness, is likewise unchanged under base restriction.

proof.text: For each $i$, $T_i$ has precisely one point $\eta_i$ above $\eta$, with residue field $k_i$. Apply local constancy of geometric component count to the proper smooth finite-presentation morphism $\overline Y_i\to T_i$. The count at $\eta_i$ is one, so there is an open neighbourhood on which all fibres are geometrically connected. Apply upper semicontinuity of proper fibre dimension to obtain an open neighbourhood on which the fibres have dimension at most one. Remove from $V$ the images under the finite maps $T_i\to V$ of the closed complements of these neighbourhoods. Those images are closed and avoid $\eta$, so this is an allowed shrinking. Thus all fibres now have both required properties. Properness plus smoothness gives finite presentation here: the objects are qcqs and smooth implies locally of finite presentation. Apply the proved simultaneous affine-shrinking lemma to these finitely many finite maps and the chosen opens.

proof.text: The generic target is finite type over K and hence Noetherian, so its supplied open W₀ is quasi-compact. The scheme-over-limit lemma identifies the generic target as the limit of its models. Descend the supplied quasi-compact marked open W₀ and its closed-immersion comparison map. Descent of closed immersion applies because this comparison, a morphism between finite-type schemes over a field, is finitely presented. Surjectivity of ν descends, and its base change to the marked open remains surjective, so the comparison is a thickening. Its inverse image in each A_i is nonempty: it is dense and A_i is nonempty. Thus it surjects onto Spec L_i. On a model the map W_i→T_i is the restriction of a smooth morphism and hence is open. Its image contains the unique point of T_i over the generic point. Remove the finite closed images of the complements of these open images, and descend the resulting shrinking through the finite radicial cover as in step 1. This gives surjectivity of every W_i→T_i. Empty index families impose no such shrinking; the empty-source surjection forces X_V empty. Apply the proved simultaneous affine-shrinking lemma to these finitely many finite maps and the chosen opens.

theorem exists_spread_marked_curve_diagram
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (η : S) (hη : ∃ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents S, IsGenericPoint η Z)
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra (S.residueField η) K]
    [Module.Finite (S.residueField η) K] [IsPurelyInseparable (S.residueField η) K]
    (n : ℕ) (L : Fin n → Type u) [∀ i, Field (L i)] [∀ i, Algebra K (L i)]
    (A B : Fin n → Scheme.{u}) (j₀ : ∀ i, A i ⟶ B i)
    (q₀ : ∀ i, B i ⟶ Spec (.of (L i)))
    (ν₀ : (∐ A) ⟶ pullback (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField η) K))))
    (hν₀ : IsFinite ν₀ ∧ Surjective ν₀)
    (hcomm : ∀ i, Sigma.ι A i ≫ ν₀ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
      j₀ i ≫ q₀ i ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (L i))))
    (hL : ∀ i, Module.Finite K (L i) ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K (L i))
    (hj₀ : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (j₀ i) ∧ Nonempty (A i))
    (hq₀ : ∀ i, Smooth (q₀ i) ∧ IsProper (q₀ i) ∧
      GeometricallyIrreducible (q₀ i) ∧ topologicalKrullDim (B i) ≤ 1)
    (W₀ : (pullback (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField η) K)))).Opens)
    (hW₀ : (∀ i, Dense ((Sigma.ι A i ≫ ν₀) ⁻¹' (W₀ : Set _))) ∧
      IsThickening (pullback.snd ν₀ W₀.ι)) :
    ∃ (U : S.Opens) (_ : η ∈ U) (V : Scheme.{u}) (g : V ⟶ U.toScheme),
      IsFinite g ∧ Surjective g ∧ UniversallyInjective g ∧
      ∃ (T Y Ybar : Fin n → Scheme.{u})
        (t : ∀ i, T i ⟶ V) (j : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ Ybar i)
        (p : ∀ i, Ybar i ⟶ T i)
        (ν : (∐ Y) ⟶ pullback f (g ≫ U.ι)),
        IsFinite ν ∧ Surjective ν ∧
        (∀ i, Sigma.ι Y i ≫ ν ≫ pullback.snd f (g ≫ U.ι) = j i ≫ p i ≫ t i) ∧
        (∀ i, IsFinite (t i) ∧ Etale (t i)) ∧
        (∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (j i)) ∧
        (∀ i, Smooth (j i ≫ p i) ∧ Surjective (j i ≫ p i)) ∧
        (∀ i, Smooth (p i) ∧ IsProper (p i) ∧
          ∀ s : T i, GeometricallyConnected ((p i).fiberToSpecResidueField s) ∧
            topologicalKrullDim ((p i).fiber s) ≤ 1) ∧
        (∃ (σK : Spec (.of K) ⟶ V)
          (hA : ∀ i, A i ⟶ Y i) (hB : ∀ i, B i ⟶ Ybar i)
          (hT : ∀ i, Spec (.of (L i)) ⟶ T i),
          σK ≫ g ≫ U.ι = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
            (algebraMap (S.residueField η) K)) ≫ S.fromSpecResidueField η ∧
          ∀ i,
            IsPullback (hA i) (j₀ i ≫ q₀ i ≫
              Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (L i))))
              (j i ≫ p i ≫ t i) σK ∧
            IsPullback (hB i) (q₀ i ≫
              Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (L i)))) (p i ≫ t i) σK ∧
            IsPullback (hT i) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (L i))))
              (t i) σK ∧
            hA i ≫ j i = j₀ i ≫ hB i ∧ hB i ≫ p i = q₀ i ≫ hT i) ∧
        ∃ W : (pullback f (g ≫ U.ι)).Opens,
          (∀ i, Surjective (((Sigma.ι Y i ≫ ν) ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι ≫ j i ≫ p i)) ∧
          IsThickening (pullback.snd ν W.ι)
